country.comment: The study examines water supply systems and hydrosocial scarcity in the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area (RJMA) and neighbouring river basins (Paraíba do Sul and Guandu) in Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Section 1; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF pp. 5–6, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Qualitative/institutional case study using descriptive secondary census and engineering data without inferential statistical estimation. Headline finding is that peripheral water deprivation is socially and institutionally constructed rather than caused by bulk drought scarcity alone.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Descriptive case-study findings show that although the 2014–2015 drought reduced Paraíba do Sul minimum flow from 190 m3/s to 110 m3/s without interrupting bulk water production at the Guandu ETA, peripheral municipalities suffer chronic hydrosocial scarcity driven by CEDAE's centralized management model, planning/investment deficits, ~40% system water losses, incomplete storage/distribution networks, and operational prioritization of core municipalities (Rio de Janeiro 98% residential network coverage in 2010; Niterói 100%) and industrial users (REDUC petrochemical complex; Queimados Industrial District receiving 200 L/s) over outlying residential districts. In the Eastern Imunana/Laranjal System (6,200 L/s produced vs. 10,900 L/s demand; 4,700 L/s deficit), 2010 coverage was 80% in São Gonçalo (~150,000 people unserved) and 27% in Itaboraí (29% via CEDAE in 2014). In the Western Guandu/Lajes/Acari System (52,400 L/s produced vs. 56,000 L/s demand in 2015; 3,600 L/s deficit), network coverage fell in Duque de Caxias from 69% (2000) to 63% (2010) and in Nova Iguaçu from 81% to 76%, and connected Baixada Fluminense districts receive water only 2–4 days per week via manual switchovers.

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 because the study is a non-experimental qualitative/institutional case study. Assigned 2 because primary semi-structured interviews with CEDAE/DAE technicians and official planning documents directly document administrative and operational mechanisms (e.g., DPA 3-day cistern reserve precondition for Minha Casa Minha Vida housing, manual distribution switchovers, industrial allocation priority, and interstate reservoir operating rule modifications) shaping water access.

sample_size.comment: The paper analyzes the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area (18 municipalities across 2 macro supply systems and 3 isolated-system municipalities) using secondary census residence totals (Tables 1–2) and qualitative semi-structured interviews with CEDAE/DAE technicians and managers, but does not report the exact count (N) of interviews conducted.
sample_size.value: 1 metropolitan area (Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area: 18 metropolitan municipalities across 2 interconnected macro water supply systems — Imunana/Laranjal serving 3 municipalities plus Paquetá Island [1,701,973 urban residents in 2010] and Guandu/Lajes/Acari serving 12 municipalities tabulated across IBGE 2000 and 2010 Censuses — and 3 municipalities with isolated systems); exact number of semi-structured interviews with CEDAE technicians and managers not reported

study_design.comment: Authors adopt Lorrain and Poupeau's (2014) multi-source water governance research methodology, triangulating official plans, diagnostic sanitation reports, descriptive secondary IBGE/engineering data, and primary semi-structured interviews with utility staff.
study_design.value: Qualitative multi-source case study (document and policy analysis, descriptive secondary census/engineering data analysis, and semi-structured interviews with utility technicians and managers following Lorrain and Poupeau 2014)
